name: ruflo
description_short: Multi-agent orchestration platform for AI coding assistants
description_long: Ruflo (formerly Claude Flow) transforms an AI coding assistant into a multi-agent environment. It deploys swarms of specialized agents (coding, testing, security, docs) that work in parallel with persistent memory and auto-learning knowledge graphs. Supports native MCP (Model Context Protocol) and includes observability and debugging tools. Ideal if you use Claude Code or Codex and want to move to a parallelized multi-agent workflow.

name: caveman
description_short: Prompt skill that reduces ~70% output tokens via telegraphic style
description_long: Caveman is a system prompt 'skill' that forces the AI to communicate in telegraphic caveman style — eliminating pleasantries, preambles, and unnecessary grammar. Result: ~65-75% reduction in output tokens, which lowers API costs and speeds up responses. Drop-in for Claude Code, Cursor, or any agent. Ideal if you pay per-token for LLM APIs and want to reduce costs without sacrificing code quality.

name: ollama
description_short: Run LLMs locally with a single command
description_long: Ollama is a runtime that lets you download, manage and run large language models (LLMs) directly on your local machine. It supports a wide range of models: Llama 3, Mistral, Gemma, Phi-3, CodeLlama, and dozens more. Installation is a single command, and running is as simple as 'ollama run llama3'. Includes a local REST API compatible with OpenAI (port 11434), CPU and GPU support (NVIDIA, AMD, Apple Silicon), and full offline operation once a model is downloaded.

name: aider
description_short: AI pair programming in your terminal, Git-native
description_long: Aider is an AI pair programming tool in the terminal that edits your files directly and makes automatic Git commits. It understands your codebase structure via tree-sitter and can modify multiple files simultaneously to implement complete features. Supports all major LLMs (OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, Ollama), includes an Architect mode (2 models for complex refactoring), voice-to-code, and the ability to add images and web pages as context.

name: fabric
description_short: Modular prompt patterns framework for augmenting human capabilities
description_long: Fabric proposes a library of 'Patterns' — modular, reusable prompts created by the community to solve specific tasks: summarize an article, extract YouTube insights, write in a precise style. Patterns can be chained into complex workflows. Model-agnostic (OpenAI, Claude, Gemini, local models) with CLI, GUI, and API integration. The massive library of crowdsourced patterns means you have a ready-to-use toolbox rather than writing prompts from scratch.

name: crewai
description_short: Framework for orchestrating role-playing autonomous AI agents
description_long: CrewAI enables you to build collaborative multi-agent pipelines where each agent has a defined role, goal, and backstory. Agents delegate tasks, share memory, and use tools (web search, code execution, file I/O) to complete complex workflows. Supports sequential and hierarchical process flows, custom tools, and integration with LangChain tools. Ideal for automating research pipelines, content generation, and software development workflows with specialized agents working in concert.

name: open-interpreter
description_short: Natural language interface to run code on your computer
description_long: Open Interpreter lets LLMs run code (Python, JavaScript, Shell, and more) locally on your machine. It gives the model a full REPL environment with filesystem access, internet access, and the ability to install packages. Interact through a ChatGPT-like terminal interface. Supports local models via Ollama as well as all major hosted LLMs. Use it to automate file organization, scrape data, create and edit media, control a browser, or any task expressible in code.

name: litellm
description_short: Unified API gateway for 100+ LLM providers with OpenAI-compatible interface
description_long: LiteLLM provides a single Python SDK and proxy server that normalizes calls to OpenAI, Anthropic, Google Gemini, Cohere, Mistral, Ollama, and 100+ other providers under one OpenAI-compatible API. Features include automatic retry with fallbacks, cost tracking per request, rate limiting, caching (Redis/in-memory), and a self-hosted proxy with a dashboard. Drop-in replacement for the OpenAI SDK — change one line to switch providers or add multi-provider fallback.

name: llama-index
description_short: Data framework for building LLM applications over your own data
description_long: LlamaIndex (formerly GPT Index) is a data framework that connects LLMs to your private data sources — PDFs, databases, APIs, Notion, Slack, and more. Provides data ingestion pipelines, vector store integrations (Pinecone, Weaviate, Chroma, pgvector), query engines, chat engines, and agent tools. Specializes in RAG (Retrieval-Augmented Generation) with advanced techniques like sentence window retrieval, recursive summarization, and hybrid search.

name: autogen
description_short: Multi-agent conversation framework by Microsoft Research
description_long: AutoGen (Microsoft Research) is a framework for building LLM applications via multi-agent conversations. Agents can be LLMs, tools, or humans and communicate to solve tasks collaboratively. Key patterns: AssistantAgent + UserProxyAgent for human-in-the-loop, GroupChat for round-robin multi-agent discussion, and nested chats for sub-task delegation. Version 0.4 introduces AgentChat API and a rewritten async core with actor-model concurrency. Supports all major LLM providers.

name: tabby
description_short: Self-hosted AI coding assistant with IDE integrations
description_long: Tabby is a self-hosted, open-source alternative to GitHub Copilot. Run a code completion server on your own hardware using models like CodeLlama, StarCoder, or DeepSeek Coder. Integrates with VS Code, JetBrains, Neovim, and Emacs via extensions. Features include fill-in-the-middle completion, repository-level context (RAG over your codebase), answer engine for code Q&A, and a web admin UI. GPU optional — runs on CPU with smaller models. Full data privacy since everything stays local.

name: whisper
description_short: OpenAI's open-source speech recognition model — transcribe and translate audio
description_long: Whisper is a general-purpose speech recognition model trained on 680,000 hours of multilingual audio. It performs transcription (audio to text in the same language) and translation (audio to English text) for 99 languages with near human-level accuracy. Available in 5 model sizes (tiny to large-v3) balancing speed and accuracy. Runs locally with no API key. Ideal for transcribing meetings, generating subtitles, building voice interfaces, or processing audio files in batch.
